title: Making Databases Faster with LLM Evolutionary Sampling

mechanism.domainTask: Physical query-plan optimization for DataFusion OLAP workloads
mechanism.populationDetail: PST-Evol maintains K independent single-plan threads; BoL-Evol maintains one current-best plan and samples K proposals per step. These are alternative search modes, not simultaneous subpopulations.
mechanism.archiveDetail: No separate persistent elite archive is described. BoL-Evol's current-best plan is its main search state; PST-Evol retains only each thread's current plan.
mechanism.replacementDetail: At each step PST-Evol advances each thread to its valid patched successor (retaining the parent on invalidity); BoL-Evol broadcasts the lowest-runtime valid successor among K trials as the next single plan, or keeps the prior plan if none are valid.
mechanism.generationDetail: Each GPT-5 call receives one previous physical plan and returns localized JSON Patch edits, typically join-side swaps or join reordering; full-plan rewriting and multi-parent fusion are not used.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: Plan validity, baseline-output equivalence, and measured latency determine whether PST retains a child or BoL selects and broadcasts it. Runtime is the scalar fitness; validity/errors are structured gates.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: PST lineage continuation is structure-based and does not compare plans across threads; BoL's next parent is the best-valid plan selected by measured runtime.

provenance.sourcePdf: papers/Making Databases Faster with LLM Evolutionary Sampling.pdf
provenance.citationWarning: The survey currently cites this work in Repeated Evaluation, a supported Chapter 6 placement (R=50 independent sandbox timings, minimum as the estimate). Other supported placements include localized JSON-Patch generation, hybrid PST/BoL population modes, staged correctness/runtime evaluation, and single-model use. LLM cardinality estimates are generation guidance, not approximate candidate evaluation.
